ko.R: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 백성 온 회중이 이렇게 말합니다. '어떻게 여러분이 이스라엘의 하나님께 이렇게 신의를 저버릴 수 있습니까? 오늘 여러분은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 떠났습니다. 여러분은 스스로 제단을 쌓았는데, 그것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 반역하는 일입니다.

decisions.choice: breach of faith: a betrayal of trust against God
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Achan's sin (7:1; verse 20): taking or doing what wrongs God, like a broken trust. The delegation repeats it in verses 20 and 22 and Phinehas in verse 31.

decisions.choice: building an altar is rebellion: sacrifice belonged at the LORD's one altar
decisions.reason: The law said Israel's offerings must be brought to the place the LORD chose, not offered at any altar (Leviticus 17:8-9; Deuteronomy 12:5-14). A second altar looked like a rival worship, and so a turning away from the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: turn back from after the LORD: stop following him
decisions.reason: To go "after" the LORD is to follow him as a people follow a leader; to turn back from after him is to give up following (Numbers 14:43; 32:15).

decisions.choice: the whole community of the LORD's people
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the congregation of the LORD" as the community of people who belong to him.

decisions.choice: "infidelidad" (L, B); "ser tan infieles" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names a breach of trust against the LORD, the same word used for Achan's sin (7:1). "Infidelidad" says that in everyday Spanish. The delegation's message stands inside their words, so it takes the inner quotation marks “ ”.

decisions.choice: "infidélité" (L, B), "être infidèles" (R) for the maal
decisions.reason: The word means breaking faith with someone one is bound to, here with the LORD. French "infidélité" says exactly that; it is used for Achan's sin in verse 20 as well.

decisions.choice: The delegation speaks to the eastern tribes as "anh em" and of themselves as "chúng tôi" / "chúng ta"
decisions.reason: They are fellow Israelites, the same people; "anh em" keeps the bond even while they accuse them. "chúng ta" includes the hearers ("our God"), "chúng tôi" leaves them out ("rebel against us").

decisions.choice: The delegation and the eastern tribes speak to each other in the formal polite style (합쇼체); Literal keeps "너희", Balanced and Readable say "여러분"
alternatives: the plain style (해라체) for the rebuke
decisions.reason: They are tribes of one people meeting as equals, and the delegation speaks for the whole congregation in a formal message. The formal polite style keeps that standing while the words carry the rebuke. "너희" at Literal follows the Hebrew "you"; "여러분" is the respectful plural of current Korean.

decisions.choice: "배신" (L, B); "신의를 저버리다" (R) for the breach of faith
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is a betrayal of trust (meaning decision m1), not sin in general; "배신" says that. The same word holds in verses 20, 22 and 31.

source.text: הַמְעַט־לָ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן פְּע֔וֹר אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־הִטַּהַ֨רְנוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְהִ֥י הַנֶּ֖גֶף בַּעֲדַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] too little for us, the iniquity of Peor, which not we have cleansed ourselves from it until this day, and came the plague on [the] congregation of Yahweh?

en.L: [Is] the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, though the plague came on the congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?
en.B: Was the sin at Peor not enough for us? To this day we have not cleansed ourselves from it, even though a plague struck the congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Remember the sin at Peor! We are still not free of it, even today. Because of it a terrible sickness struck {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people.

sw.L: [Je,] uovu wa Peori ni mdogo kwetu, ambao hatujajitakasa nao hadi leo, ingawa tauni ilikuja juu ya jumuiya ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?
sw.B: Je, dhambi ya Peori haikututosha? Mpaka leo hatujajitakasa nayo, ingawa tauni iliipiga jumuiya ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Kumbukeni dhambi ya Peori! Bado hatujawa huru nayo hata leo. Kwa sababu yake ugonjwa mbaya sana uliwapiga watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

es.L: ¿[Es] poca cosa para nosotros la iniquidad de Peor, de la cual no nos hemos purificado hasta el día de hoy, aunque vino la plaga sobre la comunidad {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?
es.B: ¿No nos bastó el pecado de Peor? Hasta el día de hoy no nos hemos purificado de él, aunque una plaga cayó sobre la comunidad {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Acuérdense|Acordaos}} del pecado de Peor! Todavía hoy no nos hemos librado de él. Por ese pecado una terrible enfermedad cayó sobre el pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Est-ce peu pour nous, la faute de Péor, dont nous ne nous sommes pas purifiés jusqu’à ce jour, et le fléau vint sur la communauté {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ?
fr.B: La faute commise à Péor ne nous suffisait-elle pas ? Jusqu’à ce jour, nous ne nous en sommes pas purifiés, bien qu’un fléau ait frappé la communauté {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Souvenez-vous de la faute commise à Péor ! Aujourd’hui encore, nous n’en sommes pas libérés. À cause d’elle, une terrible maladie a frappé le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

vi.L: Tội ác tại Phê-o há chưa đủ cho chúng ta sao, là tội mà đến ngày nay chúng ta vẫn chưa được tẩy sạch, dù tai vạ đã giáng trên hội chúng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}?
vi.B: Tội tại Phê-o chưa đủ cho chúng ta sao? Đến ngày nay chúng ta vẫn chưa được tẩy sạch khỏi tội ấy, dù tai vạ đã giáng trên hội chúng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Hãy nhớ lại tội tại Phê-o! Đến hôm nay chúng ta vẫn chưa thoát khỏi tội ấy. Vì tội ấy mà một trận dịch khủng khiếp đã giáng trên dân sự của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 브올의 죄악이 우리에게 작습니까? 우리가 오늘까지 그것에서 깨끗해지지 못하였고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 회중에 재앙이 내렸는데도 말입니다.
ko.B: 브올에서 지은 죄로는 부족하다는 말입니까? 그 일로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 회중에 재앙이 내렸는데도, 우리는 오늘까지 그 죄에서 깨끗해지지 못하였습니다.
ko.R: 브올에서 지은 죄를 기억하십시오! 우리는 오늘까지도 그 죄에서 벗어나지 못하였습니다. 그 죄 때문에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 백성에게 무서운 병이 덮쳤습니다.

decisions.choice: the iniquity of Peor: Israel's worship of Baal of Peor
decisions.reason: In Moab, Israelite men joined the Moabites in sexual sin and in the worship of Baal of Peor, and a plague killed 24,000 people before Phinehas acted (Numbers 25:1-9; Deuteronomy 4:3).

decisions.choice: is it too little for us: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question means: that sin was more than enough; must we add another?

decisions.choice: not cleansed to this day: the guilt of Peor still hung over Israel
decisions.reason: The speakers feel that Israel has not yet fully put that sin behind it, even though the plague was stopped. A new rebellion would add to an old guilt.

decisions.choice: Remember the sin at Peor!; a terrible sickness
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a call to remember, which gives the same sense in plainer words, and explains "plague" as a deadly sickness.

source.text: וְאַתֶּם֙ תָּשֻׁ֣בוּ הַיּ֔וֹם מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֗ה אַתֶּ֞ם תִּמְרְד֤וּ הַיּוֹם֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּמָחָ֕ר אֶֽל־כָּל־עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִקְצֹֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, you turn back this day from after Yahweh! And it will be, you rebel today against Yahweh, and tomorrow against all [the] congregation of Israel he will be angry.

en.L: And you, you are turning back this day from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! And it will be, [if] you rebel today against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [then] tomorrow {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.
en.B: And now you are turning away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today! If you rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today, tomorrow {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.
en.R: And now today you are turning away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! If you rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today, tomorrow {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry with all the people of Israel.

sw.L: Nanyi, mnarudi nyuma leo na kuacha kumfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Na itakuwa, [mkiasi] leo dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, [basi] kesho atakasirika na jumuiya yote ya Israeli.
sw.B: Na sasa leo mnageuka na kuacha kumfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Mkiasi dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} leo, kesho atakasirika na jumuiya yote ya Israeli.
sw.R: Na sasa leo mnamwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Mkiasi dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} leo, kesho atawakasirikia watu wote wa Israeli.

es.L: ¡Y {{plural_you:ustedes se apartan|vosotros os apartáis}} hoy de seguir {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}! Y sucederá que, [si] hoy {{plural_you:se rebelan|os rebeláis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mañana {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se enojará con toda la comunidad de Israel.
es.B: ¡Y ahora {{plural_you:ustedes se apartan|vosotros os apartáis}} hoy de seguir {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}! Si hoy {{plural_you:se rebelan|os rebeláis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mañana {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se enojará con toda la comunidad de Israel.
es.R: ¡Y ahora hoy {{plural_you:se están apartando|os estáis apartando}} {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! Si hoy {{plural_you:se rebelan|os rebeláis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mañana {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se enojará con todo el pueblo de Israel.

fr.L: Et vous, vous vous détournez aujourd’hui de {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Et il arrivera, [si] vous vous révoltez aujourd’hui contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, [que] demain {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’irritera contre toute la communauté d’Israël.
fr.B: Et maintenant, vous vous détournez aujourd’hui de {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Si vous vous révoltez aujourd’hui contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, demain {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera en colère contre toute la communauté d’Israël.
fr.R: Et maintenant, aujourd’hui, vous vous détournez {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! Si vous vous révoltez aujourd’hui contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, demain {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera en colère contre tout le peuple d’Israël.

vi.L: Thế mà anh em, ngày nay anh em quay lưng không theo {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nữa! Rồi sẽ xảy ra, [nếu] hôm nay anh em nổi loạn chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, [thì] ngày mai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nổi giận với toàn thể hội chúng Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Thế mà hôm nay anh em lại quay lưng không theo {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nữa! Nếu hôm nay anh em nổi loạn chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, thì ngày mai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nổi giận với toàn thể hội chúng Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Thế mà hôm nay anh em lại quay lưng với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Nếu hôm nay anh em nổi loạn chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, thì ngày mai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nổi giận với toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 너희는 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 따르던 데서 돌아서고 있습니다! 그리고 너희가 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 반역하면, 내일 그분께서 이스라엘 온 회중에게 진노하실 것입니다.
ko.B: 그런데 여러분은 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 따르던 데서 돌아서고 있습니다! 여러분이 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 반역하면, 내일은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 온 회중에게 진노하실 것입니다.
ko.R: 그런데 여러분은 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 떠나고 있습니다! 여러분이 오늘 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 반역하면, 내일은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 백성 모두에게 진노하실 것입니다.

decisions.choice: you rebel today ... tomorrow he will be angry: a condition and its result
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets two clauses side by side, "today you rebel ... tomorrow he will be angry", so that the first states the condition and the second what follows from it.

decisions.choice: angry with the whole congregation: one group's sin brings judgment on all
decisions.reason: Israel stands before God as one people, so the sin of some puts all at risk, as Achan's did (7:1, 11-12; verse 20).

decisions.choice: [if] ... [then]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words that show the condition, which the Hebrew leaves to the setting of the clauses.

source.text: וְאַ֨ךְ אִם־טְמֵאָ֜ה אֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶ֗ם עִבְר֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם אֶל־אֶ֨רֶץ אֲחֻזַּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר שָֽׁכַן־שָׁם֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵאָחֲז֖וּ בְּתוֹכֵ֑נוּ וּבַֽיהוָ֣ה אַל־תִּמְרֹ֗דוּ וְאֹתָ֨נוּ֙ אֶל־תִּמְרֹ֔דוּ בִּבְנֹֽתְכֶ֤ם לָכֶם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ מִֽבַּלְעֲדֵ֔י מִזְבַּ֖ח יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: But surely if unclean [is the] land of your possession, cross over for yourselves to [the] land of [the] possession of Yahweh, where dwells there [the] tabernacle of Yahweh, and take possession among us; but against Yahweh do not rebel, and us do not rebel against, by your building for yourselves an altar besides [the] altar of Yahweh our God.

en.L: But if the land of your possession is unclean, cross over to the land of the possession of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dwells, and take possession among us. But do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and do not rebel against us, by building yourselves an altar besides the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.
en.B: But if the land you possess is unclean, come over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s own land, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s tabernacle stands, and take a share of land among us. Only do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and do not rebel against us, by building an altar for yourselves other than the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.
en.R: If your land is unclean, then come across the river into {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s land, where {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tabernacle is. Take land among us. Only do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or against us. Do not build another altar for yourselves besides the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa nchi ya milki yenu ni najisi, vukeni mje katika nchi ya milki ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mahali ambapo maskani ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} inakaa, mkamiliki kati yetu. Lakini msimwasi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wala msituasi sisi, kwa kujijengea madhabahu zaidi ya madhabahu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu.
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa nchi mnayoimiliki ni najisi, vukeni mje katika nchi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mwenyewe, mahali ambapo maskani ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} imesimama, mpate sehemu ya nchi kati yetu. Ila msimwasi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wala msituasi sisi, kwa kujijengea madhabahu nyingine mbali na madhabahu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu.
sw.R: Ikiwa nchi yenu ni najisi, basi vukeni mto mje katika nchi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mahali ilipo maskani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Chukueni nchi kati yetu. Ila msimwasi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wala sisi. Msijijengee madhabahu nyingine zaidi ya madhabahu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu.

es.L: Pero si la tierra de {{plural_you:su posesión|vuestra posesión}} es impura, {{plural_you:pasen|pasad}} a la tierra de la posesión {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, donde habita el tabernáculo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} posesión entre nosotros. Pero no {{plural_you:se rebelen|os rebeléis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ni {{plural_you:se rebelen|os rebeléis}} contra nosotros, edificándose un altar aparte del altar {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios.
es.B: Pero si la tierra que {{plural_you:poseen|poseéis}} es impura, {{plural_you:pasen|pasad}} a la tierra que es {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} mismo, donde está el tabernáculo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} una parte de la tierra entre nosotros. Solamente no {{plural_you:se rebelen|os rebeléis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ni contra nosotros construyéndose otro altar fuera del altar {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}} es impura, {{plural_you:crucen|cruzad}} el río y {{plural_you:vengan|venid}} a la tierra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, donde está {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} tabernáculo. {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} tierra entre nosotros. Solamente no {{plural_you:se rebelen|os rebeléis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ni contra nosotros. No {{plural_you:se construyan|os construyáis}} otro altar aparte del altar {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} nuestro Dios.

fr.L: Mais si le pays de votre possession est impur, passez au pays de la possession {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, où demeure la Demeure {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et prenez possession au milieu de nous. Mais ne vous révoltez pas contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ne vous révoltez pas contre nous, en vous bâtissant un autel en plus de l’autel {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu.
fr.B: Si le pays que vous possédez est impur, passez dans le pays qui appartient {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, là où se trouve la Demeure {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et prenez votre part de terre au milieu de nous. Mais ne vous révoltez pas contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ne vous révoltez pas contre nous, en vous bâtissant un autel autre que l’autel {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu.
fr.R: Si votre pays est impur, alors traversez le fleuve et venez dans le pays {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, là où se trouve {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} Demeure. Prenez des terres au milieu de nous. Mais ne vous révoltez pas contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ni contre nous. Ne vous bâtissez pas un autre autel à côté de l’autel {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} notre Dieu.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu đất sở hữu của anh em là ô uế, thì hãy sang đất sở hữu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nơi Đền Tạm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ngự, và nhận phần sở hữu giữa chúng tôi. Nhưng đừng nổi loạn chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và đừng nổi loạn chống lại chúng tôi, bằng cách xây cho mình một bàn thờ ngoài bàn thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta.
vi.B: Nhưng nếu đất anh em đang sở hữu là ô uế, thì hãy sang đất của chính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nơi có Đền Tạm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và nhận một phần đất giữa chúng tôi. Chỉ xin đừng nổi loạn chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và đừng nổi loạn chống lại chúng tôi, bằng cách xây cho mình một bàn thờ khác ngoài bàn thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta.
vi.R: Nếu đất của anh em là ô uế, thì hãy qua sông sang đất của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, nơi có Đền Tạm của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Hãy nhận đất ở giữa chúng tôi. Chỉ xin đừng nổi loạn chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hay chống lại chúng tôi. Đừng xây cho mình một bàn thờ khác ngoài bàn thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng ta.

ko.L: 그러나 너희 소유의 땅이 부정하다면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성막이 머무는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 소유의 땅으로 건너와서 우리 가운데서 소유를 얻으십시오. 그러나 우리 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 제단 외에 너희를 위하여 제단을 쌓아 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 반역하지 말고, 우리에게도 반역하지 마십시오.

decisions.choice: if your land is unclean: if the land east of the Jordan is not fit for the LORD's worship
decisions.reason: The speakers allow that the eastern tribes may feel cut off from the LORD in a land without his sanctuary. The promised land proper ran to the Jordan (Numbers 34:12), and the LORD's land is the land where his tabernacle stands. If that is the fear, the answer is to move west, not to build a new altar.

decisions.choice: where the tabernacle dwells: where the LORD's dwelling-tent stands
decisions.reason: The verb "dwell" and the word "tabernacle" come from the same root. The tent is the place where the LORD lives among his people (Exodus 25:8-9), now at Shiloh (18:1).

decisions.choice: do not rebel against us: do not set yourselves against the rest of Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "rebel" with "us" in an unusual way. It may mean rebelling against the other tribes, or making them share the guilt of rebellion ("do not make rebels of us"), which fits verses 18 and 20. Either way the speakers fear the altar will divide Israel.

decisions.choice: the land you possess / your land; take a share of land among us / take land among us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words for the repeated "possession" and "take possession", which in Literal keep the Hebrew wordplay.

decisions.choice: "la Demeure" for the mishkan at every level, in this chapter
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note sets "la Demeure" at Literal and Balanced. Readable here keeps the same word, which is plain French for a dwelling, where the English Readable keeps "tabernacle". Literal keeps the Hebrew play of "dwells" and "Dwelling" with "où demeure la Demeure".

decisions.choice: "Đền Tạm" for the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant word for the tent sanctuary, the same one called "Lều Hội Kiến" in 18:1 and 19:51; the Hebrew uses a different word here, so Vietnamese does too.

decisions.choice: Achan: the man who took from the devoted things of Jericho
decisions.reason: Achan kept for himself goods from Jericho that were given over wholly to the LORD. Because of him Israel was defeated at Ai, thirty-six men died there, and his family died with him (7:1, 5, 24-26).

decisions.choice: he did not perish alone: his one sin cost other lives too
alternatives: He was one man; did he not die for his sin?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short: "and he one man; he did not perish in his iniquity." The sense is that although he was only one man, he did not die alone; others died with him and because of him. Another way to take it is as a question, "Though he was one man, did he not die for his sin?", which stresses that sin was punished. The first fits the speakers' point, that one person's sin falls on the whole people.

decisions.choice: son of Zerah: a descendant of Zerah
decisions.reason: Achan's line was "son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah" (7:1, 18). Here only the clan's founder is named.

decisions.choice: the things that belonged to the LORD alone; the LORD was angry
decisions.reason: Readable explains "devoted things" as in 7:1 and says whose wrath is meant, which the Hebrew leaves unsaid but 7:1 states.

decisions.choice: "vitu vilivyowekwa wakfu kwa maangamizi" at every level
decisions.reason: The term fixed for these books for the things devoted to the LORD by destruction (Hebrew herem). Swahili keeps the full phrase at every level, as the English keeps "devoted things"; Readable adds who they belonged to.

decisions.choice: "lo consagrado al exterminio" (L, B); "las cosas consagradas al exterminio" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for this Hebrew word: things given over wholly to the LORD, to be destroyed and never taken for oneself, as in Achan's story (chapter 7). Readable keeps the term, as the English Readable keeps "devoted things", and explains it.

decisions.choice: "les choses vouées à l'interdit" at every level
decisions.reason: The block's terms note sets "chose vouée (à l'interdit)" for the herem; the story of Achan keeps the phrase at every level, as the English keeps "devoted things". Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các vật bị nguyền để hủy diệt" for the devoted things, at every level
decisions.reason: As the terms note for Joshua sets for the Hebrew herem; the story of Achan (chapter 7) keeps the same words at every level.

decisions.choice: "진멸할 물건" for the devoted things at every level; Readable adds "주께만 속한 물건"
decisions.reason: The terms note sets "진멸할 물건" for *herem* in Joshua. Readable says what it means, things given over to the LORD alone, as the English Readable does.

vi.R: "Đấng Quyền Năng, Đức Chúa Trời, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Đấng Quyền Năng, Đức Chúa Trời, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Ngài biết sự thật, và chúng tôi muốn Y-sơ-ra-ên cũng biết. Nếu chúng tôi đã nổi loạn chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hay bất trung với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì xin đừng tha mạng chúng tôi hôm nay.

ko.L: "강하신 분, 하나님, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}! 강하신 분, 하나님, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}! 그분께서 아시니, 이스라엘도 알게 하십시오! 만일 반역으로, 또는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 배신하여 [한 일이라면], 오늘 우리를 구하지 마십시오.
ko.B: "강하신 분, 하나님, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}! 강하신 분, 하나님, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}! 그분께서 아십니다. 이스라엘도 알아주십시오! 이것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 반역하거나 배신한 일이라면, 오늘 우리를 살려 두지 마십시오.
ko.R: "강하신 분, 하나님, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}! 강하신 분, 하나님, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}! 그분께서 진실을 아십니다. 이스라엘도 그것을 알아주기를 바랍니다. 우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 반역하였거나 그분께 신의를 저버렸다면, 오늘 우리를 살려 두지 마십시오.

decisions.choice: El, Elohim, YHWH: three names of God called out together, and called out twice
alternatives: The God of gods, the LORD!
The LORD is God of gods!
decisions.reason: The tribes open their answer by crying out three names of God in a row: El, "the Mighty One", the old word for God; Elohim, "God"; and the LORD's own name. The same three open Psalm 50:1. Saying them twice makes a solemn oath: they call the God of Israel by every name to witness that they are telling the truth. The words can also be read as one title, "the God of gods, the LORD", as in Deuteronomy 10:17, or as a statement, "the LORD is God of gods". But the Hebrew here has no "of" between the first two words, as Deuteronomy 10:17 does, so this translation reads three names side by side.

decisions.choice: he knows, and Israel shall know: God is called as witness, and Israel will see the truth
decisions.reason: The tribes appeal first to God, who sees the heart, and then to Israel, who will come to know that their purpose was innocent (verses 24-28).

decisions.choice: do not save us today: a curse the speakers call down on themselves
alternatives: addressed to the delegation: do not spare us
decisions.reason: Inside the oath the speakers break off to say: if we are guilty, let no one rescue us. The words are most likely addressed to God, as part of the oath; they may also be addressed to the Israelites, meaning "then do not spare us". The sense is the same: if the charge is true, they deserve the punishment.

decisions.choice: if ... if ...: the oath continues into verse 23
decisions.reason: The "if" clauses run on into verse 23 and end with "may the LORD himself require it". That is the form of an oath: if we did this, may God punish us.

decisions.choice: The Mighty One, God, the LORD!
decisions.reason: Each level keeps three names, with "the Mighty One" for El so that it can be told apart from "God" for Elohim, as at Psalm 50:1. Readable keeps the same cry; it is short and plain enough.

decisions.choice: "Mwenye Nguvu, Mungu, BWANA"
decisions.reason: The three names of God (El, Elohim, YHWH), said twice as a solemn oath. Swahili renders El as "Mwenye Nguvu" (the Mighty One), as the English does, so that the three names stay distinct; "Mungu" alone for both El and Elohim would lose the first name.

decisions.choice: "¡El Poderoso, Dios, el SEÑOR!"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets three names of God side by side, El, Elohim and the divine name, and says them twice, as a solemn oath. Spanish keeps the three as the English does: "El Poderoso" for El, "Dios" for Elohim, and the divine name with its setting. Readable "no nos perdonen" is said to the delegation; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew singular "do not save us", spoken to God.

decisions.choice: "Le Puissant, Dieu, le SEIGNEUR !" for El, Elohim, YHWH
decisions.reason: The three names of God are cried out twice, as an oath. "Le Puissant" says what El means, as the English "the Mighty One"; "Dieu" and "le SEIGNEUR" follow the Pentateuch note.

decisions.choice: "Đấng Quyền Năng, Đức Chúa Trời, CHÚA" for the three names of God
decisions.reason: The three Hebrew names (El, Elohim, YHWH) are called out as in an oath; "Đấng Quyền Năng" keeps El apart from "Đấng Toàn Năng", which this translation keeps for Shaddai.

decisions.choice: The eastern tribes answer as "chúng tôi" and call the others "anh em"
decisions.reason: As the delegation spoke to them (verse 16).

decisions.choice: "강하신 분, 하나님, 주" for the three names called out (El, Elohim, YHWH)
decisions.reason: The three names of God are called out together, twice (meaning decision m1). "강하신 분" gives *El* as the English "the Mighty One" does, and leaves "전능하신" for *Shaddai*, as the terms note sets. The divine name keeps its setting span.

decisions.choice: The eastern tribes answer in the formal polite style (합쇼체), as the delegation spoke
decisions.reason: They speak to the priest and the leaders of Israel under oath, calling God as witness (meaning decision m2); the formal polite style fits both.

decisions.choice: burnt offering, grain offering, peace offerings: the sacrifices of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: These are the main offerings of the law: the burnt offering wholly burned (Leviticus 1), the grain offering (Leviticus 2) and the peace offerings shared in a meal (Leviticus 3). The tribes deny that their altar is for any of them.

decisions.choice: may the LORD himself require it: may God himself call us to account
decisions.reason: To "require" something from someone is to demand that they answer for it, often for blood or a broken oath (Deuteronomy 18:19; 1 Samuel 20:16). "Himself" stresses that God will be the judge.

decisions.choice: punish us
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "require", which Balanced keeps as "call us to account".

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR mismo" with no deity pronoun span
decisions.reason: Spanish says "himself" with "mismo", an adjective joined to the name, which is not a pronoun and has no capital to change, as with "Jesús mismo" in the New Testament drafts. The offerings in the terms of the Pentateuch list: "holocausto", "ofrenda de cereal", "sacrificio de paz".

decisions.choice: "của lễ thiêu", "tế lễ chay", "sinh tế bình an" for the three offerings
decisions.reason: The usual names in Vietnamese Bibles for the burnt offering, the grain offering and the peace offering, the same at every level so a reader can tell them apart.

records.literal_gloss: And if not from anxiety, from [a] matter we have done this, saying, Tomorrow will say your sons to our sons, saying, What to you and to Yahweh, [the] God of Israel?

en.L: No, out of anxiety, for a reason we have done this, thinking that tomorrow your {{gender:children|sons}} might say to our {{gender:children|sons}}, 'What [is there] to you and to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel?
en.B: No, we did it because we were worried about what might happen. We thought that someday your descendants might say to ours, 'What do you have to do with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel?
en.R: No! We did it because we were afraid of what might happen later. We thought that someday your descendants might say to our descendants, 'What right do you have to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel?

sw.L: Hapana, kwa wasiwasi, kwa sababu fulani tumefanya hivi, tukisema kwamba kesho wana wenu wangeweza kuwaambia wana wetu, 'Mna [nini] ninyi na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli?

es.L: ¡No!, sino que por inquietud, por una razón hicimos esto, pensando: Mañana {{plural_you:los hijos de ustedes|vuestros hijos}} podrían decir a nuestros hijos: “¿Qué tienen {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que ver con {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel?

es.R: ¡No! Lo hicimos porque teníamos miedo de lo que podría pasar más adelante. Pensamos que algún día {{plural_you:los descendientes de ustedes|vuestros descendientes}} podrían decirles a nuestros descendientes: “¿Qué derecho tienen {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a adorar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel?

fr.L: Non, c’est par inquiétude, pour une raison, que nous avons fait cela, en disant : demain vos {{gender:enfants|fils}} pourraient dire à nos {{gender:enfants|fils}} : “Qu’y a-t-il [entre] vous et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël ?
fr.B: Non, nous l’avons fait parce que nous étions inquiets de ce qui pourrait arriver. Nous avons pensé qu’un jour vos descendants pourraient dire aux nôtres : “Qu’avez-vous à voir avec {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël ?
fr.R: Non ! Nous l’avons fait parce que nous avions peur de ce qui pourrait arriver plus tard. Nous avons pensé qu’un jour vos descendants pourraient dire aux nôtres : “De quel droit adorez-vous {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël ?

vi.L: Không, chúng tôi đã làm điều này vì lo lắng, vì một lý do, nghĩ rằng ngày mai con cháu anh em có thể nói với con cháu chúng tôi: 'Các người có liên quan gì với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên?
vi.B: Không, chúng tôi làm điều này vì lo lắng điều có thể xảy ra. Chúng tôi nghĩ rằng một ngày kia con cháu anh em có thể nói với con cháu chúng tôi: 'Các người có liên quan gì với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên?
vi.R: Không! Chúng tôi làm điều này vì sợ điều có thể xảy ra về sau. Chúng tôi nghĩ rằng một ngày kia con cháu anh em có thể nói với con cháu chúng tôi: 'Các người có quyền gì mà thờ phượng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên?

ko.L: 아닙니다. 우리가 염려하여, 까닭이 있어서 이 일을 하였습니다. 내일 너희 자손이 우리 자손에게 '너희가 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 무슨 상관이 있느냐?
ko.B: 아닙니다. 우리는 앞일이 걱정되어서 이 일을 하였습니다. 훗날 여러분의 자손이 우리 자손에게 '너희가 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 무슨 상관이 있느냐?
ko.R: 아닙니다! 우리는 나중에 일어날 일이 두려워서 그렇게 하였습니다. 언젠가 여러분의 자손이 우리 자손에게 '너희에게 무슨 권리가 있어서 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기느냐?

decisions.choice: and if not: "no, truly", the turn from denial to the real reason
decisions.reason: In an oath "if not" means "surely" or "on the contrary". Having sworn what the altar is not for, they now say what it is for.

decisions.choice: from anxiety, from a matter: out of worry over a real concern
decisions.reason: The tribes acted from fear of something that could happen, explained in the rest of verses 24-25.

decisions.choice: tomorrow: in time to come
decisions.reason: "Tomorrow" often means the future, when children ask their parents what things mean (Exodus 13:14; Deuteronomy 6:20; 4:6 of the Jordan stones).

decisions.choice: what to you and to the LORD: you have no part with the LORD
decisions.reason: "What to me and to you?" is a way of saying two parties have nothing in common (Judges 11:12; 2 Samuel 16:10). The fear is that the western tribes would deny the eastern ones any share in Israel's God.

decisions.choice: your children/sons ... our children/sons (Literal); your descendants ... ours (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The "sons" are the future generations of both groups, men and women, so Literal uses the gender setting and Balanced says "descendants".

decisions.choice: What right do you have to worship the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the question's point, which verse 25 confirms: that the eastern tribes might be refused a place in the LORD's worship.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de ustedes" by default ("vuestros hijos" with the plural-you setting) rather than "sus hijos"
decisions.reason: With the ustedes form, "sus hijos" could be read as "their sons" or "his sons", and here "your sons" and "our sons" are set against each other, so the default spells it out as "los hijos de ustedes", as the Spanish New Testament drafts do where "su" could be misread.

decisions.choice: The imagined words of later generations are in the plain style (해라체), quoted within single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The quoted speech of descendants to descendants is a rebuff between equals, so it takes the plain style, inside the polite answer the tribes give to the delegation.

records.literal_gloss: And [a] border has put Yahweh between us and between you, [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad, the Jordan; not to you [is] [a] portion in Yahweh. And will make cease your sons our sons from fearing Yahweh.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has put a border between us and you, sons of Reuben and sons of Gad: the Jordan. [There is] no portion for you in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So your {{gender:children|sons}} would make our {{gender:children|sons}} cease to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has set the Jordan as a border between us and you, you Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' In that way your descendants could make ours stop fearing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the Jordan River a border between us and you people of Reuben and Gad. You have no share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' If that happened, your descendants might make our descendants stop worshiping {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameweka mpaka kati yetu na ninyi, wana wa Reubeni na wana wa Gadi: Yordani. Hamna fungu katika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.' Hivyo wana wenu wangewafanya wana wetu waache kumcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameufanya Yordani kuwa mpaka kati yetu na ninyi, enyi Wareubeni na Wagadi. Ninyi hamna sehemu katika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.' Kwa njia hiyo wazao wenu wangeweza kuwafanya wazao wetu waache kumcha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliufanya Mto Yordani kuwa mpaka kati yetu na ninyi watu wa Reubeni na Gadi. Ninyi hamna sehemu katika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.' Hilo likitokea, wazao wenu wangeweza kuwafanya wazao wetu waache kumwabudu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha puesto una frontera entre nosotros y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hijos de Rubén e hijos de Gad: el Jordán. No {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} parte en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”. Así {{plural_you:los descendientes de ustedes|vuestros descendientes}} podrían hacer que los nuestros dejaran de temer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} puso el río Jordán como frontera entre nosotros y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, la gente de Rubén y de Gad. {{plural_you:Ustedes no tienen|Vosotros no tenéis}} parte en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”. fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a mis une frontière entre nous et vous, fils de Ruben et fils de Gad : le Jourdain. Vous n’avez pas de part en {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.” Ainsi vos {{gender:enfants|fils}} feraient cesser nos {{gender:enfants|fils}} de craindre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a mis le Jourdain comme frontière entre nous et vous, Rubénites et Gadites. Vous n’avez pas de part {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.” Ainsi vos descendants pourraient amener les nôtres à cesser de craindre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait du Jourdain une frontière entre nous et vous, les gens de Ruben et de Gad. Vous n’avez pas de part {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.” Si cela arrivait, vos descendants pourraient amener nos descendants à cesser d’adorer {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đặt một ranh giới giữa chúng ta và các người, hỡi con cháu Ru-bên và con cháu Gát: sông Giô-đanh. Các người không có phần gì nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.' Như vậy con cháu anh em sẽ làm cho con cháu chúng tôi thôi kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đặt sông Giô-đanh làm ranh giới giữa chúng ta và các người, hỡi người Ru-bên và người Gát. Các người không có phần gì nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.' Như thế con cháu anh em có thể khiến con cháu chúng tôi thôi kính sợ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đặt sông Giô-đanh làm ranh giới giữa chúng ta và các người, dân Ru-bên và dân Gát. Các người không có phần gì nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.' Nếu điều đó xảy ra, con cháu anh em có thể khiến con cháu chúng tôi thôi thờ phượng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리와 너희, 르우벤 자손과 갓 자손 사이에 요단을 경계로 두셨다. 너희에게는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 안에 몫이 없다.' 하고 말할까 [염려하였습니다]. 그러면 너희 자손이 우리 자손으로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 경외하기를 그치게 할 것입니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리와 너희 르우벤 자손과 갓 자손 사이에 요단강을 경계로 두셨다. 너희는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 아무 몫이 없다.' 하고 말할까 걱정하였습니다. 그렇게 되면 여러분의 자손이 우리 자손에게 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 경외하지 못하게 할 것입니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 요단강을 우리와 너희 르우벤 자손과 갓 자손 사이의 경계로 삼으셨다. 너희는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 아무 몫이 없다.' 하고 말할까 두려웠습니다. 그런 일이 생기면 여러분의 자손이 우리 자손에게 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기지 못하게 할지도 모릅니다.

decisions.choice: sons of Reuben and sons of Gad: the future westerners' words to the eastern tribes
decisions.reason: In the imagined words the western descendants address the people of Reuben and Gad. Half of Manasseh is not named here, nor in verses 32-34; Reuben and Gad stand for the whole eastern group, perhaps because Manasseh also had land west of the river.

decisions.choice: a portion in the LORD: a share in belonging to the LORD and in his worship
decisions.reason: A "portion" is a share of an inheritance. To have a portion in the LORD is to belong to his people and to share in his worship; the Levites had the LORD as their portion (Deuteronomy 10:9; 18:1-2).

decisions.choice: fearing the LORD: honoring and worshiping him
decisions.reason: The fear of the LORD is reverence shown in worship and obedience (Deuteronomy 6:2, 13). Cut off from the sanctuary, later generations might stop worshiping him.

decisions.choice: you Reubenites and Gadites (Balanced); you people of Reuben and Gad (Readable)
decisions.reason: Only two tribes are named here, so Balanced and Readable name only those two, in the forms used elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.choice: stop worshiping the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "fearing" here, which is worship rather than terror (m3).
